title: Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Accounting and Reporting Standard
what_it_states: The standard that defines the fifteen Scope 3 categories, including Category 11, use of sold products. It requires the reporting company to account for the expected lifetime emissions of the products it sold in the reporting year, as an absolute quantity with no comparison to any alternative.
relation_to_ti: TI reports the same lifetime service of the same sold products, but subtracts a destination benchmark from it. The whitepaper states that TI is an addition to Category 11, not a replacement, and this is the document that fixes what Category 11 covers.

title: Technical Guidance for Calculating Scope 3 Emissions
what_it_states: The calculation guidance for each Scope 3 category. Chapter 11 gives the formulas for direct and indirect use-phase emissions of sold products, and the lifetime, use-profile and functional-unit conventions behind them.
relation_to_ti: TI's per-unit lifetime arithmetic is Category 11's arithmetic with a benchmark term subtracted; the lifetime and use-profile conventions here are the ones the TI sector guidelines have to either follow or justify departing from.

title: Carbon lock-in: types, causes, and policy implications
publisher: Annual Review of Environment and Resources 41
what_it_states: A typology of carbon lock-in: infrastructural and technological, institutional, and behavioural. It sets out why a long-lived asset commits emissions long after the decision that created it.
relation_to_ti: The concept TI's positive sign is meant to measure. A positive TI is a claim about lock-in: the asset sits above the destination's own trajectory for the rest of its life.

title: Committed emissions from existing energy infrastructure jeopardize 1.5 °C climate target
what_it_states: Computes the CO2 that existing and proposed energy infrastructure will emit over its expected operating life, by asset and country, and compares that total with the remaining carbon budget.
relation_to_ti: The closest quantitative cousin to TI's lifetime sum for power. It computes the same kind of forward lifetime total per asset, but against a global carbon budget rather than against the destination country's own trajectory, and attributes nothing to the firms behind the asset.

title: Future CO2 emissions and climate change from existing energy infrastructure
what_it_states: The original committed-emissions estimate: what the then-existing capital stock would emit if operated to the end of its normal life.
relation_to_ti: Establishes the lifetime-commitment framing TI applies per unit and per firm role.

title: Making things (that don't exist) count: a study of Scope 4 emissions accounting claims
what_it_states: Young-Ferris, Malik, Calderbank and Jacob-John examine how companies construct and report Scope 4 avoided-emissions claims, and find the counterfactual chosen by the reporting entity itself, the baseline unverifiable from the outside, and the resulting figure not additive across the firms that claim it.
relation_to_ti: The central critique TI has to answer. TI's reply is that its counterfactual is not chosen by the reporting firm but read from the destination country's own published trajectory, and that TI is never netted against Scope 3 - a reply worth only as much as the published benchmark derivation behind it.

title: CO2 Emissions Embodied in International Trade and Domestic Final Demand
what_it_states: The OECD's input-output based accounting of the production emissions embodied in traded goods, reallocating emissions from the producing country to the country of final demand.
relation_to_ti: The family TI is most often confused with, and the contrast is the point: embodied-trade accounting moves *production* emissions between countries, while TI measures the *use-phase* emissions of an exported durable asset against the destination's own trajectory. The two do not overlap and cannot be added.

title: Consumption-based carbon accounting: sense and sensibility
what_it_states: Assesses what consumption-based accounting can and cannot support as a basis for policy, including the data uncertainty and the responsibility questions it raises.
relation_to_ti: The standing critique of moving emissions between countries on paper. TI does not reallocate any country's inventory, and this reference is where that boundary should be argued.

title: NDC Registry
what_it_states: The official registry of Nationally Determined Contributions as submitted by Parties.
relation_to_ti: The source of record behind TI's S2 benchmark. The model reads NDC content through Climate Watch's structured extract and records hand rows where the structured content cannot carry the target.

title: World Energy Outlook 2024
what_it_states: The IEA's scenario set, including the Stated Policies Scenario used as an enacted-policy cross-check against stated ambition.
relation_to_ti: Named in the methodological-challenges note as the conservative cross-check for markets whose NDC cannot be turned into a benchmark. Not used as a model input: its licence does not permit republishing the series.

title: Mapping the landscape of corporate avoided emissions accounting methodologies
what_it_states: A survey and comparison of the published methodologies companies use to quantify avoided emissions, by authors who work on the attributional-consequential distinction in carbon accounting. Read here at the level of its title and scope; the full text was not retrieved.
relation_to_ti: The map of the family TI is joining. Before TI claims to improve on avoided-emissions practice it has to be placed on this map, and the comparison belongs in the positioning section the methodological-challenges note calls for.

title: Investigating comparability within corporate avoided emissions quantification
what_it_states: Examines whether corporate avoided-emissions figures produced under different methods can be compared with one another. Read here at the level of its title and scope; the full text was not retrieved.
relation_to_ti: Comparability across firms is TI's central selling point: the same benchmark is applied to every firm selling into a destination. This paper is where that claim will be tested against the field's own evidence.

title: Why Nobody Measures the Scope 4 (Avoided) Emissions? Let's Get It Started!
what_it_states: Argues that firms are increasingly asked to show their contribution beyond reducing their own Scopes 1 to 3, and proposes how a Scope 4 measurement could be started in practice.
relation_to_ti: An argument for the category TI occupies. Useful as the constructive counterweight to the critique literature, and a reminder that TI has to say plainly that its signed metric is not an avoided-emissions claim in this sense.

title: Assessing avoided carbon impacts: introducing the potential avoidance of carbon emissions through research (PACER) framework
what_it_states: Introduces a framework for assessing the carbon emissions an intervention may avoid, stated as a potential rather than a realised quantity. Read here at the level of its title and scope; the full text was not retrieved.
relation_to_ti: Part of the current wave of avoided-impact frameworks TI will be shelved beside. Its potential-versus-realised distinction is the one TI answers by reporting a distance to a published benchmark rather than a displacement claim.

title: Development of Guidelines Version 2 for Assessing Contribution of Products on Avoided Greenhouse Gas Emissions: Revision Considering the Avoided Greenhouse Gas Emissions Achieved by the Spread of Products and Services in Various Countries and Regions
publisher: Journal of Life Cycle Assessment, Japan 17(2), 62-67 (Tahara, Ubukata, Motoshita, Daigo)
what_it_states: Reports the second version of the Japanese guidelines for assessing a product's contribution to avoided greenhouse gas emissions, revised specifically to handle products and services spreading into different countries and regions.
relation_to_ti: The closest published precedent to TI's destination-specific framing, and it is Japanese, which matters because the case studies score Japanese firms. Where TI subtracts the destination's own trajectory, these guidelines make the reference vary by country and region within an avoided-emissions frame.

title: A utility-based framework for avoided emissions credit-allocation in product reuse
publisher: The International Journal of Life Cycle Assessment 31
what_it_states: Proposes how the credit for avoided emissions should be divided between the actors involved in a product's reuse, rather than granted whole to any one of them. Read here at the level of its title and scope; the full text was not retrieved.
relation_to_ti: The allocation question TI faces with several firms on one asset. TI's answer is deliberately different: it attributes the whole unit figure to each role separately and keeps the share as a column, so nothing is divided and nothing is summed across roles.

title: From Scope 3 Inventory Reductions to Grounded Emissions Consequences: A Reachability- and Evidence-Constrained Accounting Framework
what_it_states: Argues that Scope 3 accounting turns value-chain activity into additive inventory quantities but does not by itself establish how much global physical emissions changed, and proposes constraining consequence claims by what the reporting entity can actually reach and evidence.
relation_to_ti: States the inventory-versus-consequence gap TI is built in, and sets a test TI should be measured against: what part of a TI figure is a consequence the firm could reach, and what part is a distance measurement.

title: Carbon handprint - An approach to assess the positive climate impacts of products demonstrated via renewable diesel case
what_it_states: Defines the carbon handprint as the beneficial climate impact a product delivers to its user relative to a baseline solution, and works the definition through a renewable diesel case, with the baseline choice and the user-side boundary set out explicitly.
relation_to_ti: The positive-side counterpart to a footprint, and the same subtraction TI performs. The difference is whose baseline: the handprint compares against the solution the customer would otherwise have used, TI against the trajectory the destination country published.

title: The new coal champion of the world: The political economy of Chinese overseas development finance for coal-fired power plants
publisher: Energy Policy 155, 112334 (Kong, B. and Gallagher, K.P.)
what_it_states: Traces the development finance behind coal-fired power plants built overseas by Chinese institutions and the political economy that drove it, plant by plant and lender by lender.
relation_to_ti: The same object of study as the power case - a home country's institutions putting coal capacity into someone else's grid - handled as political economy rather than as emissions arithmetic. TI supplies the tonnage this literature generally leaves implicit.

title: Offshoring emissions through used vehicle exports
publisher: Nature Climate Change 14, 238-241 (Newman, Schulte, Morellini, Rahal, Leasure)
what_it_states: Links Great Britain's roadworthiness test records to export records for every used vehicle exported between 2005 and 2021, and scores the exported vehicles against two counterfactuals: vehicles scrapped at home in the same period, and the contemporary on-road fleet. Even assuming the exported vehicles function as new, they emit at least 13 per cent more per kilometre than the vehicles scrapped and 17 per cent more than the on-road fleet.
relation_to_ti: The closest published precedent to TI's export framing, and the one to cite first. It scores an exported vehicle per kilometre against a fleet-average counterfactual and frames export as offshoring a liability rather than resolving it. Three departures: the counterfactual fleet is the exporting country's rather than the destination's, the benchmark is a static observation rather than a policy trajectory, and it starts at the second transfer where TI closes at first registration. The two cover complementary halves of one vehicle's life.

title: Used Vehicles and the Environment: A Global Overview of Used Light Duty Vehicles - Flow, Scale and Regulation
what_it_states: Counts the global used light-duty vehicle trade - 14 million vehicles exported between 2015 and 2018, about 80 per cent of them to low- and middle-income countries - and maps the import rules each destination applies to age, emission standard and roadworthiness.
relation_to_ti: The flow account behind TI's export question: which vehicles leave, for where, and under what destination rules. It quantifies vehicles and standards and never tonnes, so it is cited for the flow and Newman et al. for the emissions claim.

title: Used Vehicles and the Environment: Update and Progress 2024
what_it_states: Extends the export series to 2015-2022 and adds the Republic of Korea as a fourth major exporter alongside the European Union, Japan and the United States, with the import regulatory environment for 146 countries.
relation_to_ti: Puts Korea in the exporter set the automotive case study scores, which the 2020 edition did not. Same boundary as the 2020 report: flows and rules, not emissions against a benchmark.

title: Used vehicles and CO2 emissions
publisher: KiM Netherlands Institute for Transport Policy Analysis
what_it_states: A government analytical agency asks directly whether exporting a used vehicle raises or lowers global CO2, and under which counterfactual the answer changes.
relation_to_ti: The only piece in the used-vehicle literature that treats export as a counterfactual accounting problem in TI's sense. It works from the exporting country's side; TI works from the destination's.

title: On the way to 'real-world' CO2 values? Evidence from 2021-2023 on-board fuel consumption monitoring data in the European passenger car market
publisher: International Council on Clean Transportation (Diaz, Tietge, Dornoff)
what_it_states: On-board monitoring data for roughly eight million cars registered 2021-2023. The gap between type-approval and real-world CO2 rose from 18 to 19 per cent for combustion and hybrid cars, while plug-in hybrids emitted about five times their official value in 2023, a gap that widened by half over the three years.
relation_to_ti: The current edition of the real-world correction the automotive guideline points at by an older title. It shows the correction has to be keyed on the powertrain, not on the certification cycle as the guideline currently specifies - keying on the cycle is exactly where plug-in hybrids escape.

title: From Laboratory to Road International: A comparison of official and real-world fuel consumption and CO2 values for passenger cars in Europe, the United States, China, and Japan
publisher: International Council on Clean Transportation (Tietge et al.)
what_it_states: Puts the test-cycle to real-world gap for Europe, the United States, China and Japan on one page with the basis stated per market, establishing that the gap is specific to the market and the cycle and that the values are not interchangeable.
relation_to_ti: Answers the automotive guideline's own open question about whether a European correction can be carried to Korean and Japanese specifications. The answer is that it cannot be carried without the conversion, which is why the guideline needs a per-market factor rather than one number.

title: A global comparison of the life-cycle greenhouse gas emissions of combustion engine and electric passenger cars
what_it_states: Life-cycle emissions for all powertrains in Europe, the United States, China and India, for cars registered in 2021 and 2030. It states an 18-year European lifetime, segment-specific annual mileage, annual mileage declining five per cent a year, and a grid intensity that moves over the vehicle's life so that the early years weigh most. It also states that the vehicles are assumed to stay in their region for their full life, with no allowance for export as second-hand cars.
relation_to_ti: The closest published analogue to TI's per-vehicle layer, and a comparison-vehicle metric rather than a fleet counterfactual. It contradicts two of TI's choices directly: it segments the vehicle where TI applies one scalar ratio to an all-vehicle average, and it decays distance with age where TI holds annual distance flat. Its own export exclusion is the boundary Newman et al. pick up.

title: The Global Automaker Rating 2022: Who is leading the transition to electric vehicles?
what_it_states: Scores the twenty largest manufacturers on ten metrics across six markets, including Japan and Korea, and classifies them as leaders, transitioners or laggards. The metrics are sales share, strategy and production decarbonisation on a 0-100 scale.
relation_to_ti: The nearest thing in the scoring literature to assessing one firm market by market, and it never converts to tonnes or to a destination counterfactual. It is the evidence for the claim that TI's per-destination counterfactual has no precedent in manufacturer scoring.

title: Global EV Outlook 2026
what_it_states: States its avoided-emissions method in the text: net emissions are the electricity emissions of the electric fleet less what an equivalent combustion and hybrid fleet would have emitted covering the same mileage, well to wheel, with the grid intensity moving by scenario over time.
relation_to_ti: The same-distance construction TI uses, holding mileage constant and changing what serves it. The counterfactual is the difference: the IEA compares against an equivalent new combustion vehicle, TI against the destination's whole in-use fleet of every vintage. Anyone who reads a TI figure as avoided emissions will be reading it against this definition.

title: Automotive Sector Net-Zero Standard, Version 0.1 - Second Public Consultation Draft
what_it_states: A consultation draft, not adopted. It tabulates what a sold-vehicle emissions calculation needs: cycle-to-WLTP conversions per powertrain and region, WLTP to real-world factors from European on-board monitoring, a year-by-year electricity intensity index per region to 2050 applied at country level, an 18-year passenger-car lifetime with 220,000 km, and a twenty-point annual mileage decay schedule.
relation_to_ti: Methodologically the reference implementation for three of TI's four per-vehicle choices, and the strongest published alternative to TI's mean-fleet-age lifetime and flat annual distance. It produces an intensity target against a budget share rather than tonnes against a destination, so the frameworks do not compete. Cite the version and the date: it is a draft and the numbers moved between versions.

title: Land Transport Science-Based Target-Setting Guidance, Version 1.1
what_it_states: The adopted guidance. Companies converge a well-to-wheel grams per vehicle-kilometre intensity onto a sector pathway derived from the IEA mobility model, with test cycles normalised to WLTP and a single assumed real-world gap of 1.1 applied to all regions at all times.
relation_to_ti: The sectoral decarbonisation approach applied to vehicles: a company intensity converging on a pathway, which is an alignment metric, not a counterfactual one. Its uniform 1.1 real-world factor is the error the on-board monitoring evidence has since overturned, and the initiative's own successor draft abandons it.

title: Carbon Performance Assessment of Automobile Manufacturers: Note on Methodology
what_it_states: Assesses each manufacturer's tailpipe grams per kilometre for the vehicles it sells against a sector benchmark pathway, harmonising United States and Chinese figures to WLTP with the ICCT conversion regressions.
relation_to_ti: The purest instance of sold-product intensity converging on a pathway. It is tailpipe only, so battery vehicles score zero and the destination grid never enters - the opposite of TI's treatment - and it has no destination-market resolution at all.

title: Changing Gear: Alignment of major auto manufacturers with the goals of the Paris Agreement (PACTA)
what_it_states: Measures whether manufacturers' forward production plans, by technology and unit, match the technology mix of a climate scenario over a five-year horizon, using asset-level production data.
relation_to_ti: Alignment by technology mix rather than by emissions: no emission factor, no vehicle lifetime, no grid intensity, no test cycle, and no information about where the vehicle is sold. The right citation for what alignment metrics cannot see, which is the gap TI is built for.

title: Closing the growing PHEV loophole
what_it_states: Plug-in hybrids registered in 2024 averaged 145 grams per kilometre in real use against an official 24, six times the certified value, with the private and company-car split driving much of the difference.
relation_to_ti: The empirical anchor for the plug-in hybrid utility factor the automotive guideline currently leaves as a generic band while withholding those rows. Withholding is honest but leaves a coverage hole this evidence could close.

title: Auto Environmental Guide 2023: A comparative analysis of decarbonisation efforts by global automakers
what_it_states: Ranks the fifteen largest carmakers on combustion phase-out, supply-chain decarbonisation and resource use, and adds a component crediting or penalising a carmaker's presence in markets where combustion sales persist.
relation_to_ti: That geographical component is the only place in the ranking literature that reaches for TI's destination logic, and it does so as a qualitative credit rather than an emissions counterfactual.

title: 2024 Automotive and Transportation Manufacturers Benchmark
what_it_states: Scores thirty automotive and fourteen other transport manufacturers on a low-carbon transition assessment together with just-transition and social indicators, ranking ambition, investment and management alongside performance.
relation_to_ti: An alignment and management assessment rather than a physical measurement. It answers an adjacent question to TI's and the two should be presented as complementary.

title: CDP Technical Note: Relevance of Scope 3 Categories by Sector
what_it_states: Sets out which Scope 3 categories are relevant for each sector, making use of sold products mandatory-relevant for automotive, with a generic estimation formula of units sold times lifetime times annual energy use times emission factor and no automotive-specific guidance.
relation_to_ti: The absolute-inventory pole, with no counterfactual at all, and the reason TI must never be netted against it. The absence of sector-specific guidance for automotive is part of what leaves room for a framework like TI.

title: Report from the Commission on the real-world CO2 emissions and fuel and energy consumption of new passenger cars and light commercial vehicles
what_it_states: The first regulatory report on on-board fuel consumption monitoring data, finding roughly 20 per cent real-world excess for petrol and diesel cars and about three and a half times the certified value for plug-in hybrids.
relation_to_ti: The primary source behind the real-world correction the automotive guideline leaves pending on a secondary. It is free, fleet-level and already split by powertrain, so the correction need not stay pending.

title: Vehicle Survivability and Travel Mileage Schedules (DOT HS 809 952)
publisher: National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, United States (Lu, S.)
what_it_states: Derives, from registration data, the share of vehicles of each age still in service and the distance they travel at that age, as a schedule running out to twenty years.
relation_to_ti: The ancestor of the survival-plus-mileage-decay construct that the current transport methodologies instantiate, and the citation for why a fleet's mean age is not a vehicle's lifetime. TI's automotive guideline defines a survival function and then does not use it.

title: Actions and Market Instruments Phase 1 Progress Update White Paper: purpose, principles, key concepts, and options for multi-statement reporting
what_it_states: Proposes that corporate reporting be split into four statements: a physical inventory and a market-based inventory, both attributional; a GHG impact statement based on consequential accounting, covering emissions avoided, reduced or removed by projects, interventions, investments and the production or sale of products; and non-GHG indicators. It states that the impact statement must stay clearly separated from the inventory statements, and lists the boundaries within it as an open question.
relation_to_ti: TI's home provision, if it has one. TI is a consequential metric on the sale of products, which is what the impact statement is for. The open boundary is TI's opportunity and its problem: the statement is drawn for avoided, reduced and removed, all one-signed, while TI's positive arm reports emissions added above a benchmark, a sub-category nobody has drawn yet.

title: The Greenhouse Gas Protocol for Project Accounting
what_it_states: Requires a project's baseline to be built from identified baseline candidates - the alternatives that could deliver the same product or service in the same place and period - and then estimated either project by project or as a performance standard derived from the whole population of candidates at a stated stringency level.
relation_to_ti: The formal ancestor of TI's benchmark. TI's scenarios are a performance standard in this standard's sense, and the departure is where the standard is most demanding: TI takes the benchmark from a national trajectory rather than from the population of baseline candidates, and sets its stringency at the mean or the committed path rather than at a justified percentile.

title: Policy and Action Standard: an accounting and reporting standard for estimating the greenhouse gas effects of policies and actions
what_it_states: Standardises the baseline scenario: what would most likely have happened without the policy, which other policies stay inside the baseline, how the assumptions and drivers are documented, how ex-ante and ex-post assessment differ, and how sensitivity to the baseline is reported.
relation_to_ti: TI's NDC benchmark is a policy baseline in exactly this sense, so this standard's documentation and sensitivity requirements transfer to TI wholesale. The inversion is worth stating: the standard uses a policy path as the reference for assessing that policy, TI uses it as the counterfactual for a private product.

title: Estimating and Reporting the Comparative Emissions Impacts of Products
publisher: World Resources Institute working paper (Russell, S.)
what_it_states: Frames the comparative emissions impact of a product as the difference between its life-cycle emissions and those of a reference product or situation, separates attributional from consequential framings, requires unfavourable comparisons to be disclosed alongside favourable ones, and warns against aggregating comparative claims. It deliberately does not use the term Scope 4.
relation_to_ti: The house treatment of TI's core operation, product minus reference, from the body that co-writes the GHG Protocol. TI departs by fixing the reference as a national sector trajectory rather than a competing product, which trades the reference-product selection problem for a scenario-selection problem.

title: Guidance on Avoided Emissions: helping business drive innovations and scale solutions toward net zero
what_it_states: The reference text for corporate avoided-emissions claims. Version 2.0 adds eligibility gates a claim must pass, requires an explicitly defined reference scenario, supplies disclosure templates, and adds steps for allocating a claim among the actors in a value chain. Avoided emissions are reported separately from the inventory throughout.
relation_to_ti: TI's negative arm is an avoided-emissions claim in substance whatever it is called, so these gates bind it. The sharpest difference is allocation: this guidance allocates a claim among actors so the total is not duplicated, while TI declines to allocate and keeps the share as a column.

title: Recommendation ITU-T L.1480: Enabling the Net Zero transition - assessing how the use of information and communication technology solutions impacts greenhouse gas emissions of other sectors
what_it_states: The only formally approved international-standards-body method for assessing how one sector's products change another sector's emissions, covering second-order and higher-order effects including rebound, and designed to be applied consistently from the organisation to the global scale.
relation_to_ti: The standards-body precedent for a cross-sector comparative impact metric, and the source of the requirement TI does not currently meet: rebound. TI's benchmark is a sector trajectory rather than a with-and-without system comparison, so the rebound question arrives differently, but it arrives.

title: Net Zero Initiative - The Pillar B Guide: calculating and leveraging avoided emissions
what_it_states: Sets out a three-pillar architecture in which a company reports induced emissions, avoided emissions and removals side by side and never nets them against each other, with pillar B subdivided into avoidance from the company's own operations and avoidance delivered by its products.
relation_to_ti: The cleanest precedent for reporting an impact pillar separately from the inventory, and the sharpest structural objection to TI: TI collapses induced-above-benchmark and avoided-below-benchmark into one signed number, which is precisely the netting this architecture exists to prevent.

title: Project Frame: methodology for evaluating greenhouse gas impact of early-stage investments
publisher: Project Frame, convened by Prime Coalition
what_it_states: Consensus practitioner guidance for estimating the forward-looking emissions impact of an investment, covering how to build a counterfactual, how to attribute impact to an investor rather than to the company, and how to express uncertainty at an early technology stage.
relation_to_ti: The community of practice closest to TI's finance roles, because it attributes a counterfactual impact to a financier rather than to a manufacturer. It is ex-ante on ventures where TI is ex-post on installed assets.

title: The Avoided Emissions Framework, in Towards 60 Gigatonnes of Climate Innovations (Net-Zero Innovation Module 2)
publisher: RISE Research Institutes of Sweden with Mission Innovation
what_it_states: Estimates the avoided-emissions potential of a solution against a market baseline at a target year, handling competing technologies, market penetration uncertainty and the allocation of a joint result between the technologies in an enabling solution. The edition and date could not be confirmed from the publisher's own file.
relation_to_ti: Shares the multi-actor allocation problem TI faces across its roles, and answers it by allocating where TI refuses to. It is prospective and market-level where TI is retrospective and unit-level.

title: Using attributional life cycle assessment to estimate climate-change mitigation benefits misleads policy makers
publisher: Journal of Industrial Ecology 18(1) (Plevin, Delucchi, Creutzig)
what_it_states: Argues that attributional life-cycle assessment computes a share of a static system's emissions rather than the change a decision causes, and that presenting an attributional difference as a mitigation benefit systematically misinforms. Only a consequential framing with an explicit counterfactual and a marginal system response answers the mitigation question.
relation_to_ti: The objection an assessment-literate reviewer will raise against TI's observed-trend scenario: an average reference is not a marginal one, and a difference against an average measures position, not consequence.

title: The most important GHG accounting concept you may not have heard of: the attributional-consequential distinction
what_it_states: Sets out that attributional accounting allocates a share of observed global emissions so that entity totals sum sensibly, while consequential accounting estimates the difference a decision makes against a counterfactual, and that the two use different data, answer different questions and cannot be added together.
relation_to_ti: The cleanest single citation for TI's positioning, and the sharpest warning about it: a single signed number that a reader can add to or subtract from a Scope 3 total is exactly the mixing this paper names as the field's recurring error.

title: A comparison of methodologies for avoided emissions quantification
publisher: Journal of Cleaner Production (O'Keeffe, M. and Brander, M.)
what_it_states: Applies the competing avoided-emissions methodologies to common cases and compares what they produce, which separates how much of a reported figure comes from the physical system and how much from the choice of method.
relation_to_ti: The empirical form of the objection that TI's answer is a function of its benchmark. It is the reason TI should publish its two scenarios as a range rather than as alternative point estimates.

title: The Global GHG Accounting and Reporting Standard Part A: Financed Emissions
what_it_states: Attributes a borrower's or investee's actual inventory emissions to the financier through an attribution factor - the outstanding amount over the total value of the asset or company - by asset class, including project finance, with a data-quality score reported beside every figure and avoided emissions explicitly excluded.
relation_to_ti: TI borrows the shape and breaks with it on four points: the numerator is net of a benchmark rather than gross, the share stays outside the number instead of multiplying through it, the sum is over the asset's life rather than one reporting year, and TI attributes to builders and suppliers who have no financing balance and therefore no attribution factor.

title: The Global GHG Accounting and Reporting Standard Part B: Facilitated Emissions
what_it_states: Extends attribution to capital-markets activity, where an institution arranges a transaction rather than holding it, by applying a weighting factor to the facilitated amount and requiring facilitated emissions to be disclosed separately from financed emissions.
relation_to_ti: The one place the standards world already says that arranging is a different role from holding, and prices it differently. It is the strongest precedent for TI's claim that roles are not interchangeable, and the clearest contrast: this standard resolves the difference with a discount inside the number, TI with a category beside it.

title: IFRS S2 Climate-related Disclosures
what_it_states: Requires governance, strategy, risk-management and metrics disclosures including gross Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions measured under the GHG Protocol, Scope 3 by category, and consideration of industry-based metrics, with separate volumes for automobiles and for electric utilities and power generators.
relation_to_ti: Where a client publishes its Category 11 number and its transition plan, and where TI has no home: there is no metric in this standard for a benchmarked figure. TI is supplementary information beside it, and saying so plainly is better than implying a slot exists.

title: Corporate Net-Zero Standard Version 2.0
what_it_states: Restructures Scope 3 around emissions-intensive activities with prescribed boundaries, putting sold products' use phase - including capital goods such as buildings sold by developers - inside the boundary on a well-to-wheel basis, and states that product-level avoided emissions associated with the use of sold products are not eligible for recognition under the programme.
relation_to_ti: The most direct rejection of TI's negative arm by a body a client actually reports to: a firm cannot carry a negative TI toward a validated target. The same standard's activity boundaries are close to TI's product set, so TI should at least make its product term boundary-comparable with the validated inventory.

title: Sectoral Decarbonization Approach: a method for setting corporate emission reduction targets in line with climate science
publisher: Science Based Targets initiative with CDP, WRI and WWF
what_it_states: Converges each company's emissions intensity per unit of sector activity onto a sector-wide intensity pathway derived from a global carbon budget, with the company's allocation depending on its projected activity and its distance from the sector mean.
relation_to_ti: The canonical intensity-trajectory benchmark, which is structurally what TI's observed-trend scenario is. TI makes the trajectory national and observed rather than global and budget-derived, and then converts the gap into tonnes with a sign, which this method never does.

title: PACTA for Investors Methodology Document
what_it_states: Compares a portfolio's forward-looking physical production plans in eight climate-relevant sectors against scenario pathways over a five-year horizon, allocating asset-level production to investors by ownership and reporting technology-mix alignment rather than tonnes.
relation_to_ti: TI's nearest cousin in data structure - asset level, ownership attributed, benchmarked against a scenario - and the clearest demonstration that the last step is a choice. Its designers deliberately stop before converting the deviation into tonnes; TI should say why it does not.

title: Assessing climate target alignment with cumulative benchmark divergence
publisher: Institutional Investors Group on Climate Change
what_it_states: Measures alignment as the cumulative divergence between a company's emissions and a sectoral benchmark over a period, rather than as a gap at a single future date.
relation_to_ti: Methodologically the closest published cousin to TI's integration over an asset's operating life: both sum a distance from a benchmark year by year instead of reading it once. The difference is what is summed - a company's reported emissions here, an asset's modelled emissions in TI.

title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/1818 on minimum standards for EU Climate Transition and EU Paris-aligned Benchmarks
what_it_states: Writes a decarbonisation trajectory of at least seven per cent a year, a minimum intensity reduction against the investable universe, and sector exclusions into binding law for benchmarks that carry the climate labels.
relation_to_ti: The one clear precedent for a private alignment metric being taken into law, and the warning that comes with it: the regulator had to hard-code the trajectory because the private methods would not agree on one.

title: Methodological tool: tool to calculate the emission factor for an electricity system (TOOL07)
publisher: UNFCCC Clean Development Mechanism Executive Board
what_it_states: Standardises the emission factor of the electricity a project displaces as a combined margin: the operating margin, being the plants whose generation would be affected, weighted with the build margin, being the plants whose construction would be affected, with prescribed data vintages.
relation_to_ti: TI's benchmark term is formally a grid baseline, and this is the grid baseline with twenty years of regulatory scrutiny behind it. Three departures TI should state before a reviewer does: TI applies the benchmark to a fossil unit to produce a positive number where this tool applies it to a clean one to produce a credit; TI uses a forward trajectory where this uses a historical margin; and TI makes no additionality claim. Whether TI's benchmark is closer to an operating or a build margin is a question TI has not yet answered.

title: IFI Approach to GHG Accounting for Renewable Energy Projects
publisher: International Financial Institutions Technical Working Group on GHG Accounting
what_it_states: Harmonises project-level greenhouse gas accounting across the multilateral banks: gross project emissions are estimated, then net emissions against a baseline scenario, using a common default grid emission factor dataset covering every country and, where relevant, sub-national and interconnected grids.
relation_to_ti: The identity TI computes, term for term, already in operational use. The four departures are the whole of TI's contribution: the baseline here is a static appraisal-year factor rather than a trajectory evaluated in every year of the asset's life, the figure is annual rather than lifetime, it is produced by one institution for its own portfolio rather than across every firm holding a role, and there is no role decomposition at all.

title: Joint MDB Methodological Principles for Assessment of Paris Agreement Alignment of New Operations: direct investment lending operations
publisher: Joint multilateral development banks (AfDB, ADB, AIIB, EBRD, EIB, IDB Group, IsDB, NDB, World Bank Group)
what_it_states: The operating test the multilateral banks apply before financing: whether an operation is inconsistent with the NDC of the country it takes place in, then with that country's long-term strategy, then with global sectoral pathways, the last of these recommended for operations that span countries or are closely linked to international trade. It states that the judgement is of the operation and is not a judgment or endorsement of the country's NDC.
relation_to_ti: The only operating instrument that scores a cross-border project against the destination's own NDC, which is TI's benchmark, and therefore the most important precedent in the register. It is a qualitative screen rather than a tonnage, and its first test is deliberately weak - inconsistency only where the NDC rules the operation out. Its disclaimer is the wording TI should copy.

title: Methodology to determine the Paris Agreement alignment of EBRD investments
publisher: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development
what_it_states: A worked instance of the joint methodology at one bank, with sector thresholds and the decision sequence written out.
relation_to_ti: Shows how a destination-facing alignment test is drafted so that it reads as a judgement about the operation rather than about the country - the drafting problem TI faces the moment it publishes a destination-resolved result.

title: Carbon dioxide emissions from global overseas coal-fired power plants
publisher: Nature Climate Change 14, 1151-1157 (Guo, Shen, Chen, Dai et al.)
what_it_states: Builds investment data for 908 overseas coal-fired power plants and attributes their emissions to the investor country, historically and projected forward over the plants' operating lives, separating direct emissions from those induced in the host country's wider coal fleet.
relation_to_ti: The closest published cousin: overseas assets, investor-attributed, summed over operating life. It departs exactly where TI claims to contribute - it attributes to countries rather than to named firms by role, uses one investment share rather than parallel role columns, and projects against unchanged policy rather than against the destination's own trend or committed path.

title: The Carbon Majors Database: launch report
publisher: InfluenceMap with the Climate Accountability Institute
what_it_states: Traces cumulative carbon dioxide from fossil fuel and cement production to 122 named industrial producers, classified as investor-owned, state-owned or nation states, from the mid-nineteenth century to 2022.
relation_to_ti: The intellectual ancestor of firm-level attribution: the move from country accounts to named companies is this lineage's, and TI inherits it. It attributes on the production of a fuel, gross and historical; TI attributes on roles in an asset, net of a benchmark and forward over the asset's life.

title: Carbon Bombs - mapping key fossil fuel projects
what_it_states: Identifies 425 extraction projects each capable of more than a gigatonne of lifetime carbon dioxide, and shows their combined potential exceeds the remaining budget for 1.5 degrees roughly twofold.
relation_to_ti: The same unit of analysis as TI - a named project with a lifetime total on a public register - one step earlier in the chain. Its emissions are potential, from reserves that may never be burned; TI's are modelled from an asset that is running.

title: Australia's global fossil fuel carbon footprint
what_it_states: Computes the emissions from the fossil fuels Australia exports alongside its territorial inventory, showing the exported total exceeding the domestic one, and notes that Paris accounting places those emissions in the importing country's books.
relation_to_ti: The political argument TI makes, one commodity earlier: an exporter's national inventory understates what it contributes. The distinction to draw before a reviewer draws it is that this attributes the combustion of an exported consumable, while TI attributes the operation of an exported machine.

title: Exposed: the coal insurers of last resort
publisher: Insure Our Future and Solutions for Our Climate (Bosshard, P.)
what_it_states: Names the insurers behind KEPCO's overseas coal projects - Nghi Son 2, Jawa 9 and 10, and Vung Ang 2 among them - from documents obtained through the Korean National Assembly, and tracks how much of that underwriting capacity has since exited new coal.
relation_to_ti: The closest published precedent for TI's insurer role, on exactly the projects in the result set, and the clearest demonstration of the gap: it attributes underwriting capacity, never a tonne, with no benchmark and no lifetime.

title: Public Finance for Energy Database
what_it_states: A transaction-level record of energy finance from the G20 bilateral development institutions, the G20 export credit agencies and the major multilateral banks, covering roughly fourteen thousand transactions since 2008.
relation_to_ti: The best public source for the lender and cover roles TI records, and the clearest statement of what is missing: it records committed dollars per transaction and has no emissions layer. TI is, in one framing, the emissions join onto this table.

title: Quantifying the shift of public export finance from fossil fuels to renewable energy
what_it_states: Assembles 921 export-credit-backed energy deals across 31 countries from 2013 to 2023 and tracks the shift of export credit from fossil fuels toward renewables, with the destination mix that came with it.
relation_to_ti: The peer-reviewed benchmark for building a defensible deal-level export-credit dataset, and it stops one step short of TI: it measures finance volumes and technology mix, never the emissions those deals enabled.

title: Statement on International Public Support for the Clean Energy Transition (the Glasgow Statement), administered as the Clean Energy Transition Partnership
what_it_states: Signatory governments and institutions commit to end new direct public support for the international unabated fossil fuel energy sector, with limited exceptions they define as consistent with 1.5 degrees, and to prioritise support for the clean energy transition.
relation_to_ti: The instrument that closes the forward pipeline TI measures, which is why TI's value is retrospective: the statement stops new flows, TI assesses the stock already built and still running.

title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2738 carrying the Arrangement on Officially Supported Export Credits
what_it_states: The export-credit rulebook Japan and Korea participate in, as transposed into EU law. It prohibits officially supported export credits for new coal-fired electricity plants, and gates support elsewhere on project class and technology.
relation_to_ti: The negative result that frames TI's policy case: the rulebook conditions export support on what the technology is, never on where the destination's emissions are headed. No export credit instrument anywhere applies the destination-trajectory test the multilateral banks apply to themselves.

title: Regulation (EU) 2023/956 establishing a carbon border adjustment mechanism
what_it_states: Charges importers of cement, iron and steel, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity and hydrogen for the emissions embedded in the goods they bring into the European Union, against the price of the Union's own allowances.
relation_to_ti: The other direction of travel, and the contrast worth stating: this reaches across the border for the emissions embedded in making an imported good, against the importing bloc's own carbon price. TI looks at the emissions an exported good will cause in use, against the destination's own trajectory.

title: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories, Volume 1, Chapter 1
publisher: IPCC Task Force on National Greenhouse Gas Inventories
what_it_states: Sets the territorial rule for national inventories: emissions and removals taking place within national territory and the offshore areas a country has jurisdiction over. For road transport it states that fuel use is counted in the country where the fuel is sold, not where the vehicle is driven.
relation_to_ti: The rule that decides whose books an exported product's emissions land in, and a correction TI has to absorb: a vehicle's emissions follow the fuel sale, so they land in the destination only while the vehicle is fuelled there.

title: Paris Agreement (Articles 4 and 6)
publisher: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, as published in OJ L 282
what_it_states: Article 4 makes accounting for a nationally determined contribution the Party's own act and requires the avoidance of double counting. Article 6 makes the use of internationally transferred mitigation outcomes voluntary and subject to authorisation by the participating Parties.
relation_to_ti: The provision that governs TI's negative numbers. An avoided tonne inside a destination's territory is that country's to count unless it authorises a transfer, so a TI contribution is a measurement, never a claim on anyone's target - and the framework has to say so in those words.

title: Committed emissions from existing and planned power plants and asset stranding required to meet the Paris Agreement
publisher: Environmental Research Letters 13, 054019 (Pfeiffer, Hepburn, Vogt-Schilb, Caldecott)
what_it_states: Extends the committed-emissions calculation to planned as well as existing power plants and quantifies how much of the capital stock would have to be stranded for the Paris goals to hold.
relation_to_ti: The closest published construction to TI's lifetime sum for power: per plant, forward, to the end of economic life. It benchmarks against a global carbon budget rather than the destination's own grid, and attributes to nobody.

title: Quantifying operational lifetimes for coal power plants under the Paris goals
publisher: Nature Communications 10, 4759 (Cui, Hultman, Edwards et al.)
what_it_states: Uses plant-level data in an integrated assessment model to derive the operating lifetimes coal units would need under well-below-two-degree and 1.5-degree pathways, resolved by country and by unit vintage.
relation_to_ti: The best-sourced defence of whatever operating life TI assumes, and the input that most moves TI's lifetime sum. TI's sensitivity should be run against these lifetimes rather than against a flat bracket.

title: Commitment accounting of CO2 emissions
publisher: Environmental Research Letters 9, 084018 (Davis, S.J. and Socolow, R.H.)
what_it_states: Proposes reporting, alongside annual emissions, the future emissions committed by the capital assets brought into service in that year - a commitment ledger by vintage.
relation_to_ti: The precedent for TI's vintaging: the commitment is booked in the year the asset is sold or commissioned, which is also Category 11's convention. TI departs by netting the commitment against a benchmark where this proposal reports it gross.

title: Assessing carbon lock-in
publisher: Environmental Research Letters 10, 084023 (Erickson, Kartha, Lazarus, Tempest)
what_it_states: Separates lock-in from the committed emissions of physical capital, from the cost of later abatement, and from institutional and behavioural entrenchment, and proposes indicators for each.
relation_to_ti: The vocabulary that lets TI call a positive figure a lock-in liability defensibly, and the limit on that claim: TI measures one of the three channels and should not imply the others.

title: Consumption-based accounting of CO2 emissions
what_it_states: Quantifies the carbon dioxide embodied in international trade with a global input-output model, finding that roughly a quarter of global emissions in 2004 were released making goods consumed in another country.
relation_to_ti: The founding paper of the family TI is most often confused with. It re-labels production emissions that have already occurred, leaving the global total unchanged and needing no counterfactual; TI models use-phase emissions that occur later in the destination and subtracts a benchmark, so it can be negative and carries counterfactual uncertainty.

title: Consumption-based carbon accounting: does it have a future?
publisher: WIREs Climate Change 8(1), e438 (Afionis, Sakai, Scott, Barrett, Gouldson)
what_it_states: Reviews the case for consumption-based accounting against its methodological complexity and political infeasibility, and examines which adjustments could survive contact with actual policy.
relation_to_ti: The standing critique of any accounting that moves emissions off the territorial basis. TI moves nothing between national inventories, and that boundary is worth stating against this literature rather than leaving a reader to assume otherwise.

title: 2022 Concept Note on Portfolio Alignment Measurement
publisher: Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero
what_it_states: Reviews how portfolio alignment metrics are built - binary target measures, benchmark divergence, implied temperature rise - documents the attempts to converge them, and records the divergence that remains between credible methods applied to the same companies.
relation_to_ti: The family TI structurally belongs to, and its own record of the problem TI inherits: two defensible methods score the same firm differently, which is the first thing a regulator asks about any new alignment metric.

title: EV progress report 2026
what_it_states: Scores each carmaker pool against the European Union's own manufacturer CO2 target for the 2025 to 2027 period, decomposing the levers each is using to comply - battery-electric share, plug-in hybrids, conventional hybrids and pooling.
relation_to_ti: The same structure as TI at the market level, a firm scored against a destination trajectory, with two differences that matter: the trajectory is a legally binding target on that manufacturer's new registrations rather than a national fleet counterfactual, and the metric is compliance in grams per kilometre rather than lifetime tonnes.

title: Automakers and Climate Policy Advocacy: a global analysis
what_it_states: Pairs a score for each automaker's climate-policy advocacy with its forecast zero-emission production share to 2030 against a 1.5-degree trendline, including a separate assessment of Chinese and Japanese automakers' policy engagement in the emerging markets they export to.
relation_to_ti: Assesses the same firms in the same destination markets TI scores, and measures a different object entirely: lobbying posture rather than emissions. It is the clearest demonstration that destination-resolved corporate assessment exists without anyone converting it to tonnes.
